newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-FOCUS-Re-opening Bougainville seen as big job.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-FOCUS-Re-opening Bougainville seen as big job.

text.p: Re-opening the crisis-torn Bougainville copper-gold mine would take between 12 months and many years, analysts contacted by Reuters said on Monday.

Their assessments followed a statement by Papua New Guinea Prime Minister Sir Julius Chan that his government would approach the RTZ Corp Plc-CRA Ltd group to purchase its 53.6 percent stake in Bougainville Copper Ltd.
Analysts showed a great divergence of views on time and cost in the possible reopening of the Panguna mine.

The mine's eight-year closure after being overrun by secessionist rebels in May 1989 made it virtually impossible to estimate what needed to be done to resume production, they said. The mine would require a minimum ten months for re-erection of plant and 12 months before it could begin production, while a "proper" re-opening, backed by full preparation and studies, would take 12 to 24 months, one analyst said.
Bougainville Copper chairman David Karpin said in a recent report that initial studies indicated production could be re-started within 18 months from a return to the island.
Other analysts said a re-opening could take three to four years. One said it would take "quite a while".
Not that Bougainville rebels were giving much comfort that a re-opening of the mine was likely soon, if at all.
"We closed the CRA mine in 1989 and it will remain so until a political agenda for the people of Bougainville is settled," rebel spokesman Moses Havini said in Sydney on Monday.
CRA declined to comment on whether it would be interested in re-opening the mine, given the opportunity, or on what time-frame and cost might be involved if it did.
"I wouldn't give you a response," CRA spokesman Ian Head said. "We've got no proposal from the government and it would not be appropriate for us to respond if anyone else was re-opening the mine."
Analysts said CRA would be very likely to re-open the mine if it were given the opportunity to do so.
After the mine's long closure, it was not known if a re-opening would require starting from scratch, nor if new machinery was needed, analysts said.
In 1991 Bougainville Copper made a 350 million kina (US$252 million) provision for deterioration of assets. A resumption of operation could entail a further major write-down, Karpin said.
Cost of returning the mine to full production was estimated at the upper end of a range between 400 million kina and 600 million kina, he said.
Analysts and CRA's Head would not comment on the possible cost of re-opening the mine.
"We're just waiting to see what this proposal is he's (Chan is) talking about," Head said.

The Bougainville mine, formerly CRA's greatest prize, between opening in 1972 and closure in 1989, produced copper concentrate containing three million tonnes of copper, 306 tonnes of gold and 784 tonnes of silver for a total production value of 5.2 billion (kina.
This represented about 44 percent of PNG's total annual exports and amounted to about 17 percent of the country's internally generated revenue.
Recoverable ore reserves at the end of 1995 were unchanged at 496 million tonnes of average grade 0.42 percent copper and 0.55 grams per tonne of gold.
The PNG government already owns 19.1 percent of Bougainville Copper, with the remaining 27.3 percent held by the public.
CRA shares closed at A$18.80, down by 49.2 cents from Friday's close, while Bougainville Copper shares closed at 58 cents, up two cents.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
